text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000115 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, with much of it on low-complexity patients, but records came back for too few 99215 claims to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern: the 99215 share runs several times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry routine diagnoses such as uncomplicated hypertension, obesity, rash and low back pain (e.g., C0048846, C0048895, C0048912), and some patients repeat at 99215 (M0020634, M0020571). The documentation does not support that concern, but it is too thin to judge: only 2 documented 99215 claims exist, and both were supported, including C0049020, a single-condition depression visit documented as high MDM. The 3 notes claiming moderate-plus data review with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence of possibly templated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, prioritizing repeat patients M0020634 and M0020571, and check whether the MDM and time documentation reflects what actually happened at the visit."}
